target.title: fix(web-fetch): recover from stale runtime providers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runtime web-fetch metadata can retain a selected provider id that is no longer available in the current provider list. When the user did not explicitly configure that provider, resolution returned no provider instead of falling back to the current auto-detected provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resolver now treats an explicit `providerId` as authoritative and fail-closed, while allowing stale runtime `selectedProvider` metadata to fall back to auto-detection. This keeps explicit config strict without letting old runtime state disable web fetch.

## User Impact

Users recover web fetch automatically after provider metadata becomes stale, while invalid explicit provider configuration still fails clearly.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-vitest-cache-web-content-rebase node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/web-content-core/src/provider-runtime-shared.test.ts`
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on `packages/web-content-core/src/provider-runtime-shared.ts` and `packages/web-content-core/src/provider-runtime-shared.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- Claude autoreview: clean after rebase to `upstream/main`

## Proof

The regression tests cover stale runtime metadata falling back to the current provider and an explicit missing provider still returning no provider.
